findings.F1: Inside the profile (628 of 2,436 bars, 26 %), no feature I measured predicted a short-side move that stood out from chance. Across 9 features in round 1 and 7 in round 2, each at horizons of 1, 2, 3 and 5 days (about 60 tests), the strongest falling pattern was the upper wick's top tercile at 3 days: −3.13 % against drift, t −1.79, 202 cases. With that many tests, this is chance level.
findings.F2: The tested situation's own grading was absent at the idea's 3-day horizon in this explore half. The scaled 3-day rise's top tercile earned +0.11 % unusual move over 3 days (t 0.05, 129 cases), and its slope t was −0.56. The 5-day horizon was positive but not sure: top tercile +4.28 %, t 0.99, 83 cases; Spearman rho 0.218, p 0.048.
findings.F3: The only slopes with t above 2 were on the long side, at 5 days, on 83 cases: the upper wick times the day's scaled rise (t 2.39) and the candle body (t 2.20). Both point to rises, not falls, so neither serves the short box, and neither survives the number of angles looked at.
findings.F4: In-profile unusual 3-day moves were negative in 8 of 9 windows. w16 was the exception at +2.96 % on 62 cases. The pooled mean of about −0.7 % on 202 cases is small, depends on one window and has no graded situation behind it.
findings.F5: Weekday effects were not distinguishable from zero. The weakest day was Wednesday, at −1.21 % over 1 day (t −1.43, 94 cases).
findings.F6: In the book, bars in a position averaged +0.57 % (t 1.44, 168 bars). Trade returns ran against the forecast: the lowest entry-forecast tercile averaged +13.7 % net and the highest +4.8 % (30 trades each). These means are carried by a few large ZEC trades (ZEC mean +12.1 % against a median of +3.1 %, 50 trades), so they are not a stable short-side pattern.

no_ideas: None of the patterns I examined in rising agitated markets on the short side stood out from chance. I looked at the scaled 1, 3, 7 and 10-day rises, close location, wide range, upper wick, opening gap, body, volume ratio, distance to the 20-day high, the 60-day return, weekdays, windows, coins and trades, at 1 to 5 days; the strongest falling pattern had t −1.79 across about 60 tests.
